To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The non‐lymphocytic cell population is composed of T‐zone histioctyes, Langerhans' cells, dendritic reticulum (DR) cells and macrophages.

T‐zone histocytes and particularly LCH were abundant in all CTCLs but also found in BCLs, T‐zone histioytes were associated with T lymphocytes, particularly Th but not with T8 lymphocytes, DR cells were essentially confined in well‐differentiated GC and macrophages occurred both in lymphomas and pseudolympomas without any definite relationship with either lymphocytes or T lymphocytes.

‘T‐zone histiocytes and Langerhans' cells were abundant in cutaneous T‐lymphomas and B‐cell lymphomatoid papulosis, but were also present, though to a lesser extent, in B‐cell follicular lymphomas, whereas dendritic reticulum and macrophage cells were present in all cutaneous lymphoprolliferative diseases, irrespective of their histopathology.’
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of non‐lyphoid ‘accessory cells in the pathogenesis of cutaneous lymphomas and pseudoliymphomas.
the significance of non‐lymphotypic cells in the skin in the pathogenesis of lymphomas.
the co‐distribution and significance of non‐lymphotyic accessory cells in cutaneous lymphomas and pseudohmphomas of the skin.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
non‐lymphocyte accessory cells in cutaneous lymphomas and pseudotumours do not represent specific diagnostic features.
non‐lymphocytes in the skin are associated with lymphocytes in the T‐cell lymphoma and pseudolymphoma but are not in the B‐cell lymphomatous infiltrate.
T‐zone histioctyes are associated with T‐helper cells and that dendritic reticulum and macrophages are not associated with any lymphocyte subset in cutaneous malignant lymphomas.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
T‐zone histiocytosis is a constant finding in cutaneous T‐lymphomas, whereas dendritic reticulum cell proliferation is characteristic for B‐cell lymphoproliferations of low grade malignancy.
the co‐distribution pattern of non‐lympoid cells in cutaneous lymphopoplerative disorders is different from that of the corresponding nodal lymphomas.
the distribution pattern of non‐lymphotyic accessory cells in cutaneous lymphopoplerative diseases is not related to the type of lymphoid cells involved, but rather to the degree of malignancy.
The main takeaway from our work is that

non‐lymphocyte cells, particularly Langerhants cells, are abundant in all cutaneus T‐cell lymphoma and B‐cell lymphomata, and may have an important role in lymphocyte activation and in the pathogenesis of lymphoproliferation.
non‐lymphocytes are not only a normal component of lymphoid tissues but also a part of malignant lymphomas and their pseudolymphomatous counterparts.
the distribution of accessory cells is a useful diagnostic tool for cutaneous lymphoma and pseudolymphoma.
